newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rebels report protests against food shortage.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rebels report protests against food shortage.

text.p: Civilians in Sri Lanka's northern rebel heartland organised marches this week to protest against an alleged food siege of the region by the government, Tamil Tiger separatists said on Friday.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said in a statement that protest marches were held in the northern Wanni region, which is mostly under rebel control.

Foreign and local aid agencies had criticised the government for disrupting food supplies at a meeting held in northeastern Mullaitivu, which was also attended by representatives of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), it said.

"Most NGO (non-governmental organisations) representatives in attendance openly stated that despite repeatedly presenting the government with facts and figures relating to the desperate food shortage among the Wanni displaced, they had met with deliberate government obstructions to carrying out relief work," the statement said.
But a UNHCR official told Reuters in Colombo that he had no information about such a meeting. An ICRC spokesman was not immediately available for comment.

The UNHCR official, however, confirmed that thousands of people, displaced in the on-going and previous military offensives, had marched in northwestern Mannar district protesting against the food situation.
"Our representative in Madu (in Mannar district) says there were 2,000 people at the march," the official said.

The LTTE have accused the Sri Lankan military, which launched a huge offensive against the separatists in May to open a strategic northern highway through the brush jungle of the Wanni, of not allowing food into the region.
But a government spokesman told Reuters on Friday that more than 6,000 tonnes of food and other essential items had been sent to the Wanni in the past month.

"More than 600 lorries, each carrying 10 tonnes of food and other supplies, have been sent to Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu, Mannar and Vavuniya in the Wanni under the escort of the ICRC," the spokesman said.
Sri Lanka has said that there has been no change in the government's policy of sending all essential supplies required by the people in the rebel-conrolled areas.

The Foreign Ministry said last month that Sri Lanka had never used food as a weapon in its war against the rebels, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
